figures.caption: Fig. 1: Overview of the study. We use CHAP weights pretrained on hip accelerometer data from a prior study, then finetune them on iWatch wrist / hip accelerometer data for the same sitting versus non-sitting classification task.
TABLE III: Test set performance metrics across participants.

TABLE II: Confusion matrices for sitting versus non-sitting across 10-second windows. Top row: CHAPFT; bottom row: ViTSmall. Left: hip; right: wrist. Each entry represents the fraction of samples for a given actual class that are predicted as the corresponding class.
TABLE IV: Agreement of hip-worn CHAPZS, CHAPFT, ViTSmall, and ActiGraph 100 cpm cut point with SenseCam for sedentary behavior metrics across participants
TABLE V: Agreement of wrist-worn CHAPZS, CHAPFT, ViTSmall, and ActiGraph 1853 cpm cut point with SenseCam for sedentary behavior metrics across participants

Fig. 5: CHAPFT prediction heatmaps for subject i067A with hip placement (top figure) and wrist placement (bottom figure). Yellow band: wear log. Hot Pink band: non wear segments (extracted from ActiGraph via the Choi algorithm). Black: Vector Magnitude per minute from ActiGraph. Solid bars: posture labels. Ground truth activities are shown in the upper half, and prediction results are shown in the lower half.

Fig. 6: Data augmentation: a seven-minute sample of tri-axial accelerometer data is shown in its original form followed by four types of augmentations added step by step: scaling, channel permutation, axis rotation, and jittering.
